source_title: MLC election results: NDA wins 16, Congress draws blank, SP gets 5 in UP; state-wise results and key wins - The Times of India
source_excerpt: NEW DELHI: Congress faced a major setback in the legislative council elections on Wednesday, failing to secure a victory in the seats declared so far across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Maharashtra, even as counting continued in several constituencies.The biggest setback for the Congress came in Karnataka, where it failed to win a single seat despite being in power in the state. The BJP-JD(S) alliance swept all four legislative council seats, with the BJP retaining three constituencies and the JD(S) wresting the Bengaluru Teachersâ seat from the Congress. The defeat was particularly significant for the ruling party as it lost its sitting seat in Bengaluru Teachersâ and failed to make gains in any of the three BJP-held constituencies.In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP and Samajwadi Party (SP) registered wins, while in Bihar, Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party opened its legislative council account by defeating the Congress. The RJD also scored a victory in Bihar, wresting the Patna Teachersâ seat from the BJP.Counting for 28 legislative council seats across Uttar Pradesh (11), Bihar (8), Maharashtra (5) and Karnataka (4) began on Tuesday following polling on October 23. The elections were held for graduatesâ and teachersâ constituencies, with results declared for several seats and counting continuing in others.Here is a state-wise look at the latest results and counting trends.Karnataka (4 seats): BJP-JD(S) alliance sweeps all four, Congress draws blankThe BJP-JD(S) alliance swept all four legislative council seats in Karnataka, dealing a setback to the ruling Congress. The BJP retained the North-East Teachersâ, South-East Graduatesâ and West Graduatesâ constituencies, while its ally JD(S) wrested the Bengaluru Teachersâ seat from the Congress.JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated sitting Congress MLC Puttanna by 908 votes in Bengaluru Teachersâ. Ranganath secured 10,810 votes against Puttannaâs 9,902.BJPâs Shashil G Namoshi retained North-East Teachersâ by 3,297 votes, securing his fifth victory from the constituency with 15,596 votes against Congress candidate Sharanappa Matturâs 12,299.In South-East Graduatesâ, BJP candidate K M Suresh defeated Congress nominee Shashi Hulikunte Mutt by 23,098 votes. Sitting BJP MLC S V Sankanur retained West Graduatesâ, defeating Congress candidate Mohan Limbikai by 9,323 votes.The results marked a clean sweep for the opposition alliance, with the Congress failing to win a single seat despite campaigning by chief minister D K Shivakumar, former chief minister Siddaramaiah and other senior leaders.However, the results are not expected to affect the stability of the Congress government or significantly alter the balance of power in the 75-member Legislative Council.Uttar Pradesh (11 seats): BJP wins four seats, SP secures twoThe BJP won six of the 11 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council seats, while the Samajwadi Party secured five. The BJP won the Agra Graduatesâ, Bareilly-Moradabad Teachersâ, Lucknow Teachersâ, Meerut Teachersâ, Meerut Graduatesâ and Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachersâ constituencies.The Samajwadi Party won the Allahabad-Jhansi Graduatesâ, Varanasi Teachersâ and Agra-Aligarh Teachersâ constituencies.In the Agra Graduatesâ constituency, BJP candidate Manvendra Pratap Singh (Guruji) was declared elected.The BJP retained the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachersâ seat, with its candidate Hari Singh Dhillon defeating SP nominee Danish Akhtar by 17,676 votes. Dhillon secured 21,672 votes against Akhtarâs 3,996 after all five rounds of counting.The BJP also won the Lucknow Teachersâ constituency, where its candidate Umesh Dwivedi defeated SPâs Sushil Kumar by 6,992 votes. Dwivedi secured 13,179 votes against Kumarâs 8,371.In Meerut, the BJP won both the Teachersâ and Graduatesâ constituencies. Its candidates Dinesh Kumar Goyal and Shri Chand Sharma were declared winners in the Graduatesâ and Teachersâ seats, respectively.The BJP also retained the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Teachersâ constituency, with its candidate Dhruv Tripathi defeating Independent candidate Rajiv Yadav by 307 votes. Tripathi secured 14,887 votes against Yadavâs 14,580.However, Yadav alleged that the election had been manipulated to ensure his defeat. Claiming that around 1,000 votes had been stolen, he said he would approach the Election Commission and the court to challenge the result. He also demanded a forensic examination of 1,612 votes counted in the fourth round, alleging irregularities in the counting process.The MLC polls are being viewed as a prestige battle between the ruling BJP and the opposition SP ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Voting for the 11 seats, comprising five Graduatesâ and six Teachersâ constituencies, was held on Friday, with counting beginning at 8 am on Tuesday.Bihar (8 seats): Jan Suraaj opens account, RJD defeats BJP veteranThe Bihar Legislative Council elections delivered several upsets, with five sitting MLCs losing their seats and the Jan Suraaj Party securing its maiden victory in the Upper House.Of the eight seats, which went to polls on October 23, the BJP won three, Independents secured two, while the RJD, Jan Suraaj Party and NDA partner JD(U) won one seat each.Jan Suraaj Party candidate Suresh Prasad Rai defeated sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha in the Darbhanga Teachersâ constituency, marking the partyâs first win in the Bihar Legislative Council.BJP candidate Narendra Prasad Singh won the Tirhut Teachersâ seat, defeating CPI MLC Sanjay Kumar Singh, who had the support of the INDIA bloc.In another major upset, RJD candidate Sanjeev Kumar defeated veteran BJP MLC Nawal Kishore Yadav in the Patna Teachersâ constituency, ending the latterâs long hold on the seat.Independent candidate Rahul Raj also defeated sitting MLC Afaq Ahmed in the Saran Teachersâ constituency.Meanwhile, JD(U)âs Neeraj Kumar retained the Patna Graduatesâ seat for a fourth consecutive term, defeating his rivals despite a challenge from within his party. BJP candidates Sarvesh Kumar and N K Yadav retained the Darbhanga Graduatesâ and Kosi Graduatesâ seats, respectively.Independent candidate Bansi Dhar Brajwasi also retained the Tirhut Graduatesâ constituency, while two other seats went to the BJP and Independents as part of the overall tally.The Congress, which contested five seats, failed to win any and is now left with just one member in the 75-member Bihar Legislative Council.The polls saw 90 candidates contesting four Graduatesâ constituencies and 60 candidates in four Teachersâ constituencies. The four Graduatesâ seats had 4.92 lakh eligible voters, while the four Teachersâ constituencies had 40,253 voters.Maharashtra (5 seats): Congress retains Nagpur graduatesâ seat, defeats BJPThe BJP-led ruling Mahayuti won two seats in Maharashtra, while the opposition NCP (SP) bagged two, as results were declared for all five Legislative Council seats.Congress candidate and sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari defeated BJPâs Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes to retain the Nagpur Division Graduatesâ constituency, ending more than 40 hours of counting. Wanjari secured 67,231 votes against Kohaleâs 63,960.Also read: Congress opens account in MLC polls as Abhijit Wanjari retains Nagpur seat after nail-biting contestKohale, a former MLA, had led Wanjari by 4,294 votes after the second round of counting on Wednesday. However, with no candidate securing the required quota through first-preference votes, the counting proceeded to second-preference votes, allowing Wanjari to overtake his rival during the elimination rounds.Shiv Sena candidate Kiran Sarnaik won the Amravati Teachersâ constituency, while BJP candidate Kaustubh Gawade emerged victorious in the Pune Teachersâ constituency.In the Pune Graduatesâ constituency, NCP (SP) candidate Harshada Deshmukh-Jadhav won, while party candidate Pratapsinh Patil secured victory in the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) Graduatesâ constituency.The polls, held on October 23, saw 182 candidates contesting across three Graduatesâ and two Teachersâ constituencies.
